tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

content.content:
1	# Feature Specification: P-RF05 — Personal summary export
2	
3	**Feature Branch**: `010-personal-summary-export` (spec directory only — no git branch was created automatically; none of this repo's extension hooks are configured)
4	
5	**Created**: 2026-10-24
6	
7	**Status**: Draft
8	
9	## Clarifications
10	
11	### Session 2026-10-24
12	
13	- Q: What should the export sheet show when the job fails entirely (FR-007 — no data produced at all, not just the AI narrative), given the prototype only defines an "Erro" state for the narrative-only failure and has no visual for this harder case? → A: Generic failure message (reusing the error color/icon family, with copy distinct from FR-006's narrative-only explanation), no PDF/raw buttons, and only the existing "Fechar" link — no dedicated in-sheet retry control, and the same text is shown regardless of the backend's specific errorCode. Retrying means closing the sheet and tapping the download icon again (FR-011's existing path) (resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I).
14	
15	**Input**: User description: "P-RF05 — Personal summary export: Let the user export a narrative summary of their entries as PDF, and always be able to download the raw data. Requirement and acceptance criteria: docs/input/requirements.md, section 1, RF05. Prototype states: the export sheet — 'Pendente', 'Processando', 'Concluído', 'Erro', 'Período vazio' (prototype extract, section 2.5); opened by the download icon of Meus Registros. Screen ↔ job status mapping: docs/input/backend/export-screen-states.md. Backend: POST /export/summary, GET /export/:jobId/status, GET /export/:jobId/download. Depends on: RF07. Do not implement features of later units, extension features (requirements, section 2), or change the backend."
16	
17	## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*
18	
19	### User Story 1 - Getting a narrative PDF of your entries (Priority: P1)
20	
21	From My Records, the user taps the download icon and asks to export a summary of their entries. They watch the export prepare and then generate an AI narrative, and end up with a PDF they can download that tells the story of that period, alongside their original entries.
22	
23	**Why this priority**: This is the entire premise of RF05 — a narrative export is the feature's main value. Without it reaching a downloadable PDF, the feature does not exist.
24	
25	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by opening the export sheet for a period that has at least one entry, letting the job run to completion, and confirming a PDF download succeeds and contains a narrative summary.
26	
27	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
28	
29	1. **Given** the user is on My Records with at least one entry in the exported period, **When** they tap the download icon, **Then** the export sheet opens and shows "Pendente" (spinner, "Preparando exportação...").
30	2. **Given** the export sheet is showing "Pendente", **When** the backend starts generating the AI narrative, **Then** the sheet shows "Processando" ("Gerando resumo com IA...", progress bar) without the user doing anything further.
31	3. **Given** the job finishes with both the data and the narrative ready, **When** the sheet updates, **Then** it shows "Concluído" (green check, "Resumo pronto") with two enabled buttons — "Baixar PDF" (primary) and "Baixar dados brutos" (outline).
32	4. **Given** the sheet is showing "Concluído", **When** the user taps "Baixar PDF", **Then** the app downloads a PDF file containing the generated narrative summary for that period.
33	
34	---
35	
36	### User Story 2 - Your raw data is never held hostage by the AI narrative (Priority: P1)
37	
38	Generating the narrative summary can fail — the AI call can time out or error out. When that happens, the user can still get their own data out: the export sheet explains that only the narrative failed and lets them download their raw entries anyway.
39	
40	**Why this priority**: Called out explicitly as its own acceptance criterion ("a failure generating the narrative text still allows downloading the raw data without the narrative — the export is not blocked by an AI failure"). Without this, a flaky AI call would make a user's own data unreachable, which is a trust-breaking failure for a personal-data feature.
41	
42	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by forcing the narrative generation to fail (e.g., simulating an AI timeout) for a period that does have entries, and confirming the sheet still offers — and completes — a raw-data download.
43	
44	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
45	
46	1. **Given** the export job's data finished successfully but the narrative generation failed or was skipped, **When** the sheet updates, **Then** it shows "Erro" (red warning) with text explaining that the AI summary failed but the data remains available, and exactly one enabled button — "Baixar dados brutos" (no "Baixar PDF" option is shown).
47	2. **Given** the sheet is showing this "Erro" state, **When** the user taps "Baixar dados brutos", **Then** the download succeeds with the user's raw entry data, with no dependency on the narrative ever having completed.
48	3. **Given** the export job fails entirely (not only the narrative — no data was produced either), **When** the sheet updates, **Then** it shows a failure state with no download option at all, which is visibly a harder failure than the narrative-only case in Scenario 1 (nothing is available to download because nothing was produced).
49	
50	---
51	
52	### User Story 3 - Exporting a period with nothing in it is handled gracefully (Priority: P2)
53	
54	The user requests an export for a period that turns out to have zero entries. Instead of an empty or broken PDF, or the app hanging, they get a clear message telling them there is nothing to export.
55	
56	**Why this priority**: Called out explicitly as an acceptance criterion ("an export job with zero entries in the period returns a handled error state — not an empty PDF, not a crash"). It is a correctness guarantee as much as a UX one.
57	
58	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by requesting an export for a period known to contain zero entries and confirming the sheet shows the dedicated empty-period state immediately, with no job ever appearing to run and no file ever offered for download.
59	
60	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
61	
62	1. **Given** the user selects a period with zero entries, **When** they request the export, **Then** the sheet shows "Período vazio" ("Nenhum registro nesse período." plus a suggestion to adjust the filter) directly — never "Pendente" or "Processando" first — and offers no download button.
63	2. **Given** the sheet is showing "Período vazio", **When** the user taps "Fechar", **Then** the sheet dismisses without having created any downloadable file and without affecting My Records' own list or filters.
64	
65	---
66	
67	### Edge Cases
68	
69	- The user taps "Fechar" while the job is still "Pendente" or "Processando": the sheet dismisses and the in-flight job is left alone server-side; the app does not keep polling it in the background once the sheet is gone, and it is not treated as the "current" export if the sheet is reopened.
70	- The user taps the download icon again while an export sheet/job from a previous tap is still in flight for the same period: this does not create a second concurrent export job — the tap is treated as a no-op (or reopens the same in-flight sheet) rather than firing a second `POST /export/summary`.
71	- The session expires while the export sheet is open: the existing expired-session overlay (RF07) takes over exactly as it does for the rest of the screen; once re-authenticated, the sheet resumes reflecting the export job's real status rather than being stuck mid-attempt.
72	- The download itself (PDF or raw data) fails after the job reached a downloadable state (e.g., the signed URL expired or the connection drops mid-download): the corresponding button returns to a retryable state rather than leaving the sheet stuck or silently failing.
73	- Opening the export sheet, polling its job, or downloading a file does not alter My Records' list, its active filters, its sync badges, or its scroll position in any way.
74	- Opening My Records itself, its filters, its tags, the chat, the dashboard, or any other screen or action not named in this feature: unaffected by this unit and not touched by it.
75	
76	## Requirements *(mandatory)*
77	
78	### Functional Requirements
79	
80	- **FR-001**: A download icon in My Records' header MUST open the export bottom sheet.
81	- **FR-002**: Opening the export sheet MUST request an export for the period currently represented by My Records' active date filter (or the full history if no date filter is applied), including the narrative by default.
82	- **FR-003**: If the requested period contains zero entries, the sheet MUST show the "Período vazio" state immediately — never "Pendente" or "Processando" first — with no download control offered and no job left running.
83	- **FR-004**: For a period with at least one entry, the sheet MUST show "Pendente" (spinner, "Preparando exportação...") immediately after the request, then transition to "Processando" ("Gerando resumo com IA...", progress bar) while the job is still working toward a result, without requiring any user action to advance between these states.
84	- **FR-005**: When the job's data and narrative both complete successfully, the sheet MUST show "Concluído" with two enabled controls — "Baixar PDF" (primary) and "Baixar dados brutos" (outline).
85	- **FR-006**: When the job's data completes but the narrative generation fails or is skipped, the sheet MUST show "Erro" with text explaining that the AI summary failed while the data remains available, and exactly one enabled control — "Baixar dados brutos" — with no PDF option offered.
86	- **FR-007**: When the job fails entirely (no data produced, not only the narrative), the sheet MUST show a failure state with a generic message explaining the export itself could not be generated — text distinct from FR-006's narrative-only explanation, shown the same way regardless of the backend's specific error code — no download control at all, and only the "Fechar" link available (no dedicated in-sheet retry control; retrying means closing the sheet and tapping the download icon again, per FR-011). This state MUST be visually and functionally distinct from FR-006's narrative-only failure.
87	- **FR-008**: "Baixar PDF" MUST only ever be offered when FR-005's conditions hold, and tapping it MUST download a PDF containing the generated narrative for the exported period.
88	- **FR-009**: "Baixar dados brutos" MUST be offered in both the FR-005 and FR-006 outcomes, and tapping it MUST download the user's raw entry data for the exported period, independent of whether the narrative ever succeeded.
89	- **FR-010**: A "Fechar" link MUST be present and functional in every one of the five sheet states ("Pendente", "Processando", "Concluído", "Erro", "Período vazio"), dismissing the sheet without cancelling any in-flight backend job and without affecting My Records' own list, filters, or scroll position.
90	- **FR-011**: Repeated taps on the download icon, or on a download button that already has a request in flight, MUST NOT create multiple concurrent export jobs or fire duplicate download requests for the same action.
91	- **FR-012**: If the session expires while the export sheet is open, the existing session-expiration handling (RF07) MUST take over exactly as it does elsewhere on the screen, and the sheet MUST resume reflecting the export job's actual status once re-authenticated rather than remaining stuck.
92	- **FR-013**: This unit MUST NOT implement manual-tag or category filtering, or any other extension feature (requirements, section 2); MUST NOT implement functionality belonging to units later than RF05 in the build order; and MUST NOT modify the backend, its API contract, or its configuration.
93	
94	### Key Entities
95	
96	- **Export Job**: An ephemeral, user-scoped job created by one export request, covering one period of entries. Carries an overall status (preparing / generating / data-ready-without-narrative / fully done / failed) and a narrative status that advances independently of it (pending / generating / done / failed / skipped), since the raw data and the AI narrative can finish — or fail — on different timelines. Produces, at most, two downloadable artifacts (a PDF narrative and the raw data) once it reaches a state where either is available. It is not a journal entry and is never shown anywhere outside the export sheet.
97	
98	## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*
99	
100	### Measurable Outcomes
101	
102	- **SC-001**: A user exporting a period that has at least one entry can reach a downloaded, readable narrative PDF end-to-end, with zero crashes and zero empty or malformed files, across all tested periods.
103	- **SC-002**: In 100% of forced narrative-failure cases (for a period with entries), the user still completes a raw-data download from the same sheet, with a clear explanation of what happened.
104	- **SC-003**: Exporting a period with zero entries is communicated through a single, clear sheet state in 100% of tested cases, with zero downloadable files ever produced and zero crashes.
105	- **SC-004**: Closing the export sheet, from any of its five states, leaves My Records' list, active filters, and scroll position completely unchanged in 100% of tested cases.
106	- **SC-005**: No export attempt — successful, narrative-failed, fully failed, or empty-period — ever leaves the sheet showing a "preparing" or "generating" indicator indefinitely; every attempt reaches one of its defined terminal states within the system's normal response time.
107	
108	## Assumptions
109	
110	- **Period selection**: The export sheet exports whatever period My Records' own active date filter currently represents (or the entire history, if no date filter is applied) rather than offering a separate period picker inside the sheet itself — the prototype's export sheet shows no period-selection control of its own, and My Records already owns date filtering (RF06/RF07).
111	- **Narrative inclusion**: Every export request includes the narrative by default (there is no prototype control to opt out of it upfront) — a request only ends up "without narrative" when generation fails or is skipped, never by the user's deliberate choice.
112	- **When downloads become available**: The two download buttons appear only once the job reaches one of the sheet's defined terminal states — "Concluído" or "Erro" — matching the prototype's literal five-state catalog. # Feature Specification: P-RF05 — Personal summary export

**Feature Branch**: `010-personal-summary-export` (spec directory only — no git branch was created automatically; none of this repo's extension hooks are configured)

**Created**: 2026-10-24

**Status**: Draft

## Clarifications

### Session 2026-10-24

- Q: What should the export sheet show when the job fails entirely (FR-007 — no data produced at all, not just the AI narrative), given the prototype only defines an "Erro" state for the narrative-only failure and has no visual for this harder case? → A: Generic failure message (reusing the error color/icon family, with copy distinct from FR-006's narrative-only explanation), no PDF/raw buttons, and only the existing "Fechar" link — no dedicated in-sheet retry control, and the same text is shown regardless of the backend's specific errorCode. Retrying means closing the sheet and tapping the download icon again (FR-011's existing path) (resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I).

**Input**: User description: "P-RF05 — Personal summary export: Let the user export a narrative summary of their entries as PDF, and always be able to download the raw data. Requirement and acceptance criteria: docs/input/requirements.md, section 1, RF05. Prototype states: the export sheet — 'Pendente', 'Processando', 'Concluído', 'Erro', 'Período vazio' (prototype extract, section 2.5); opened by the download icon of Meus Registros. Screen ↔ job status mapping: docs/input/backend/export-screen-states.md. Backend: POST /export/summary, GET /export/:jobId/status, GET /export/:jobId/download. Depends on: RF07. Do not implement features of later units, extension features (requirements, section 2), or change the backend."

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Getting a narrative PDF of your entries (Priority: P1)

From My Records, the user taps the download icon and asks to export a summary of their entries. They watch the export prepare and then generate an AI narrative, and end up with a PDF they can download that tells the story of that period, alongside their original entries.

**Why this priority**: This is the entire premise of RF05 — a narrative export is the feature's main value. Without it reaching a downloadable PDF, the feature does not exist.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by opening the export sheet for a period that has at least one entry, letting the job run to completion, and confirming a PDF download succeeds and contains a narrative summary.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the user is on My Records with at least one entry in the exported period, **When** they tap the download icon, **Then** the export sheet opens and shows "Pendente" (spinner, "Preparando exportação...").
2. **Given** the export sheet is showing "Pendente", **When** the backend starts generating the AI narrative, **Then** the sheet shows "Processando" ("Gerando resumo com IA...", progress bar) without the user doing anything further.
3. **Given** the job finishes with both the data and the narrative ready, **When** the sheet updates, **Then** it shows "Concluído" (green check, "Resumo pronto") with two enabled buttons — "Baixar PDF" (primary) and "Baixar dados brutos" (outline).
4. **Given** the sheet is showing "Concluído", **When** the user taps "Baixar PDF", **Then** the app downloads a PDF file containing the generated narrative summary for that period.

---

### User Story 2 - Your raw data is never held hostage by the AI narrative (Priority: P1)

Generating the narrative summary can fail — the AI call can time out or error out. When that happens, the user can still get their own data out: the export sheet explains that only the narrative failed and lets them download their raw entries anyway.

**Why this priority**: Called out explicitly as its own acceptance criterion ("a failure generating the narrative text still allows downloading the raw data without the narrative — the export is not blocked by an AI failure"). Without this, a flaky AI call would make a user's own data unreachable, which is a trust-breaking failure for a personal-data feature.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by forcing the narrative generation to fail (e.g., simulating an AI timeout) for a period that does have entries, and confirming the sheet still offers — and completes — a raw-data download.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the export job's data finished successfully but the narrative generation failed or was skipped, **When** the sheet updates, **Then** it shows "Erro" (red warning) with text explaining that the AI summary failed but the data remains available, and exactly one enabled button — "Baixar dados brutos" (no "Baixar PDF" option is shown).
2. **Given** the sheet is showing this "Erro" state, **When** the user taps "Baixar dados brutos", **Then** the download succeeds with the user's raw entry data, with no dependency on the narrative ever having completed.
3. **Given** the export job fails entirely (not only the narrative — no data was produced either), **When** the sheet updates, **Then** it shows a failure state with no download option at all, which is visibly a harder failure than the narrative-only case in Scenario 1 (nothing is available to download because nothing was produced).

---

### User Story 3 - Exporting a period with nothing in it is handled gracefully (Priority: P2)

The user requests an export for a period that turns out to have zero entries. Instead of an empty or broken PDF, or the app hanging, they get a clear message telling them there is nothing to export.

**Why this priority**: Called out explicitly as an acceptance criterion ("an export job with zero entries in the period returns a handled error state — not an empty PDF, not a crash"). It is a correctness guarantee as much as a UX one.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by requesting an export for a period known to contain zero entries and confirming the sheet shows the dedicated empty-period state immediately, with no job ever appearing to run and no file ever offered for download.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the user selects a period with zero entries, **When** they request the export, **Then** the sheet shows "Período vazio" ("Nenhum registro nesse período." plus a suggestion to adjust the filter) directly — never "Pendente" or "Processando" first — and offers no download button.
2. **Given** the sheet is showing "Período vazio", **When** the user taps "Fechar", **Then** the sheet dismisses without having created any downloadable file and without affecting My Records' own list or filters.

---

### Edge Cases

- The user taps "Fechar" while the job is still "Pendente" or "Processando": the sheet dismisses and the in-flight job is left alone server-side; the app does not keep polling it in the background once the sheet is gone, and it is not treated as the "current" export if the sheet is reopened.
- The user taps the download icon again while an export sheet/job from a previous tap is still in flight for the same period: this does not create a second concurrent export job — the tap is treated as a no-op (or reopens the same in-flight sheet) rather than firing a second `POST /export/summary`.
- The session expires while the export sheet is open: the existing expired-session overlay (RF07) takes over exactly as it does for the rest of the screen; once re-authenticated, the sheet resumes reflecting the export job's real status rather than being stuck mid-attempt.
- The download itself (PDF or raw data) fails after the job reached a downloadable state (e.g., the signed URL expired or the connection drops mid-download): the corresponding button returns to a retryable state rather than leaving the sheet stuck or silently failing.
- Opening the export sheet, polling its job, or downloading a file does not alter My Records' list, its active filters, its sync badges, or its scroll position in any way.
- Opening My Records itself, its filters, its tags, the chat, the dashboard, or any other screen or action not named in this feature: unaffected by this unit and not touched by it.

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-001**: A download icon in My Records' header MUST open the export bottom sheet.
- **FR-002**: Opening the export sheet MUST request an export for the period currently represented by My Records' active date filter (or the full history if no date filter is applied), including the narrative by default.
- **FR-003**: If the requested period contains zero entries, the sheet MUST show the "Período vazio" state immediately — never "Pendente" or "Processando" first — with no download control offered and no job left running.
- **FR-004**: For a period with at least one entry, the sheet MUST show "Pendente" (spinner, "Preparando exportação...") immediately after the request, then transition to "Processando" ("Gerando resumo com IA...", progress bar) while the job is still working toward a result, without requiring any user action to advance between these states.
- **FR-005**: When the job's data and narrative both complete successfully, the sheet MUST show "Concluído" with two enabled controls — "Baixar PDF" (primary) and "Baixar dados brutos" (outline).
- **FR-006**: When the job's data completes but the narrative generation fails or is skipped, the sheet MUST show "Erro" with text explaining that the AI summary failed while the data remains available, and exactly one enabled control — "Baixar dados brutos" — with no PDF option offered.
- **FR-007**: When the job fails entirely (no data produced, not only the narrative), the sheet MUST show a failure state with a generic message explaining the export itself could not be generated — text distinct from FR-006's narrative-only explanation, shown the same way regardless of the backend's specific error code — no download control at all, and only the "Fechar" link available (no dedicated in-sheet retry control; retrying means closing the sheet and tapping the download icon again, per FR-011). This state MUST be visually and functionally distinct from FR-006's narrative-only failure.
- **FR-008**: "Baixar PDF" MUST only ever be offered when FR-005's conditions hold, and tapping it MUST download a PDF containing the generated narrative for the exported period.
- **FR-009**: "Baixar dados brutos" MUST be offered in both the FR-005 and FR-006 outcomes, and tapping it MUST download the user's raw entry data for the exported period, independent of whether the narrative ever succeeded.
- **FR-010**: A "Fechar" link MUST be present and functional in every one of the five sheet states ("Pendente", "Processando", "Concluído", "Erro", "Período vazio"), dismissing the sheet without cancelling any in-flight backend job and without affecting My Records' own list, filters, or scroll position.
- **FR-011**: Repeated taps on the download icon, or on a download button that already has a request in flight, MUST NOT create multiple concurrent export jobs or fire duplicate download requests for the same action.
- **FR-012**: If the session expires while the export sheet is open, the existing session-expiration handling (RF07) MUST take over exactly as it does elsewhere on the screen, and the sheet MUST resume reflecting the export job's actual status once re-authenticated rather than remaining stuck.
- **FR-013**: This unit MUST NOT implement manual-tag or category filtering, or any other extension feature (requirements, section 2); MUST NOT implement functionality belonging to units later than RF05 in the build order; and MUST NOT modify the backend, its API contract, or its configuration.

### Key Entities

- **Export Job**: An ephemeral, user-scoped job created by one export request, covering one period of entries. Carries an overall status (preparing / generating / data-ready-without-narrative / fully done / failed) and a narrative status that advances independently of it (pending / generating / done / failed / skipped), since the raw data and the AI narrative can finish — or fail — on different timelines. Produces, at most, two downloadable artifacts (a PDF narrative and the raw data) once it reaches a state where either is available. It is not a journal entry and is never shown anywhere outside the export sheet.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: A user exporting a period that has at least one entry can reach a downloaded, readable narrative PDF end-to-end, with zero crashes and zero empty or malformed files, across all tested periods.
- **SC-002**: In 100% of forced narrative-failure cases (for a period with entries), the user still completes a raw-data download from the same sheet, with a clear explanation of what happened.
- **SC-003**: Exporting a period with zero entries is communicated through a single, clear sheet state in 100% of tested cases, with zero downloadable files ever produced and zero crashes.
- **SC-004**: Closing the export sheet, from any of its five states, leaves My Records' list, active filters, and scroll position completely unchanged in 100% of tested cases.
- **SC-005**: No export attempt — successful, narrative-failed, fully failed, or empty-period — ever leaves the sheet showing a "preparing" or "generating" indicator indefinitely; every attempt reaches one of its defined terminal states within the system's normal response time.

## Assumptions

- **Period selection**: The export sheet exports whatever period My Records' own active date filter currently represents (or the entire history, if no date filter is applied) rather than offering a separate period picker inside the sheet itself — the prototype's export sheet shows no period-selection control of its own, and My Records already owns date filtering (RF06/RF07).
- **Narrative inclusion**: Every export request includes the narrative by default (there is no prototype control to opt out of it upfront) — a request only ends up "without narrative" when generation fails or is skipped, never by the user's deliberate choice.
- **When downloads become available**: The two download buttons appear only once the job reaches one of the sheet's defined terminal states — "Concluído" or "Erro" — matching the prototype's literal five-state catalog. The backend can report an intermediate state where the raw data is ready but the narrative is still generating; this unit treats that intermediate state as still part of "Processando" visually (no early download link appears mid-generation), since the prototype defines no sixth state for it and the acceptance criteria ("the export is not blocked by an AI failure") are fully satisfied once "Erro" exposes the raw-data download — nothing in the source material requires exposing it earlier than that.
- **Full job failure vs. narrative-only failure**: These are treated as two distinct outcomes (see FR-006 vs. FR-007) because the backend distinguishes them (an overall failed job produces no data at all, so there is nothing to download) — the prototype's single "Erro" state is understood to describe the narrative-only failure specifically, since its own text says the data remains available.
- **Resuming an export after leaving the sheet**: Closing "Fechar" does not cancel the underlying job, but this unit does not add a job-history or notification feature for jobs left running in the background — the prototype has no such affordance. Reopening the export sheet afterward is a fresh request; it does not need to return to a leftover job.
- **File handling on download**: "Baixar PDF" and "Baixar dados brutos" trigger the platform's standard way of saving or sharing a downloaded file; this unit is not responsible for building a custom in-app file viewer.
- **Status polling**: The exact interval at which the sheet checks `GET /export/:jobId/status` while "Pendente"/"Processando" is an implementation detail, not a product requirement, as long as it is frequent enough that the user does not perceive the sheet as stuck.

24	# Cerne Constitution
25	
26	## Core Principles
27	
28	### I. Product Source of Truth
29	`docs/input/` — `requirements.md`, `prototype/`, and `backend/` — is the
30	authoritative source for product behavior. `requirements.md` defines
31	functional and quality requirements, screens, the API surface, delivery
32	order, and technical constraints; `prototype/` is the frozen visual
33	reference and its token/state extract; `backend/` documents the existing
34	API, error taxonomy, screen-state map, sync-badge semantics, and fixtures.
35	Where these documents are silent, implementers MUST make a reasonable
36	technical decision rather than block on clarification. Files under
37	`docs/input/` are frozen inputs and MUST NOT be edited by anyone working in
38	this repository.
39	
40	Rationale: a reflective-journaling app with a frozen, already-documented
41	backend has exactly one place where ambiguity should be resolved — the
42	product input — so decisions stay traceable and the backend contract stays
43	stable.
44	
45	### II. Fixed Technology Stack
46	The app is built with Flutter and Dart at the version pinned via `fvm`,
47	using `flutter_bloc` for state management and Clean Architecture with three
48	layers per feature. Error handling MUST use `fpdart`, with every repository
49	returning `Either<Failure, T>`. Test doubles MUST use `mocktail`. Speech-to-
50	text runs on-device via `whisper_ggml`; audio content MUST NEVER be sent to
51	the backend. The shipping platform is iOS. Choices not fixed here — routing,
52	HTTP client, local cache, dependency injection, secure storage, biometrics,
53	and charting — are open implementation decisions.
54	
55	Rationale: a single, non-negotiable stack removes a whole category of
56	architectural debate and keeps the codebase consistent across features
57	built by different contributors or at different times.
58	
59	### III. Backend Boundary — Frozen Backend, No Direct AI Calls
60	The backend is already built and frozen. The app consumes it strictly as
61	documented in `docs/input/backend/`, including its API contract
62	(`docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`); the app MUST NOT change the
63	backend, its API contract, or its configuration. All AI features, including
64	semantic search, are provided exclusively by the backend — the app MUST
65	NEVER call an AI provider directly. Configuration and credentials come from
66	a project-root `.env` with exactly two variables: `FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL` and
67	`SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`. Every call to `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<function>` MUST
68	carry the header `apikey: <SUPABASE_ANON_KEY>`. The `Authorization: Bearer`
69	header carries `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` for operations that need no user session
70	(sign-up, login, refresh) and the user's access token for every operation
71	marked `bearerAuth` in the OpenAPI contract. `.env` and any credential MUST
72	NEVER be committed.
73	
74	Rationale: the backend and its AI integrations are out of this project's
75	scope and already relied upon elsewhere; treating them as an immutable,
76	narrowly-accessed contract prevents scope creep and accidental coupling or
77	credential leakage.
78	
79	### IV. Design Token Discipline & Visual Fidelity
80	`lib/core/design_tokens.dart` is the single source of colors, typography,
81	spacing, and radii. No visual value MAY be hardcoded anywhere else. The UI
82	MUST be faithful to `docs/input/prototype/`. UI text MUST be in Portuguese,
83	exactly as written in the prototype; code identifiers, comments, and project
84	documentation MUST be in English.
85	
86	Rationale: a single token source makes visual fidelity (RNF08) mechanically
87	checkable, and separating UI language (Portuguese, matching the frozen
88	prototype) from code language (English) keeps the codebase reviewable while
89	preserving the product's voice.
90	
91	### V. Clean Architecture Folder Convention
92	Code MUST follow the folder convention:
93	```
94	lib/
95	  core/
96	  features/
97	    <feature>/
98	      data/
99	      domain/
100	      presentation/
101	```
102	The domain layer MUST comply with RNF06: zero layer violations — it MUST
103	NOT import `package:flutter` nor any class from a feature's `data/` layer.
104	
105	Rationale: a fixed, enforced folder shape and a flutter/data-free domain
106	layer make the domain independently testable and keep business rules
107	portable regardless of UI or persistence choices.
108	
109	## Quality Standards (RNF01–RNF09)
110	
111	These targets from `docs/input/requirements.md` are binding quality gates:
112	
113	- **RNF01 — Interaction latency**: a local action MUST be reflected in the
114	  UI in under 100 ms; any network call taking longer than 300 ms MUST show a
115	  loading indicator.
116	- **RNF02 — PII stripping**: performed backend-side via Claude Haiku 4.5
117	  with a structured prompt / tool use, not a dedicated NER model; the app
118	  implements no PII-detection logic of its own.
119	- **RNF03 — Zero data retention**: a backend-side policy; the app MUST NOT
120	  introduce its own retention beyond what the backend requires.
121	- **RNF04 — Row Level Security (RLS)**: enforced backend-side; the app MUST
122	  assume RLS is authoritative and MUST NEVER attempt to bypass it.
123	- **RNF05 — Hard delete of account and data (LGPD)**: the app MUST expose
124	  the account-deletion flow (`DELETE /account`) from Settings.
125	- **RNF06 — Zero layer violations**: see Principle V; 0 violations is the
126	  target.
127	- **RNF07 — Domain test coverage**: `lib/**/domain/**` MUST reach at least
128	  80% test coverage.
129	- **RNF08 — Visual fidelity**: every screen MUST match the prototype's
130	  color, typography, and spacing, with 0 hardcoded visual values outside
131	  `design_tokens.dart`.
132	- **RNF09 — Consistent network-error handling**: every repository MUST use
133	  the `Either<Failure, T>` pattern via `fpdart`; every write endpoint (5
134	  endpoints) MUST handle timeout, malformed response, and no-connection
135	  failures, each covered by `mocktail` tests (15 of 15 scenarios).
136	
137	## Scope & Delivery Boundaries
138	
139	- Functional requirements MUST be implemented in the delivery order given in
140	  `docs/input/requirements.md`.
141	- Extension features (section 2 of `requirements.md`) are explicitly out of
142	  scope and MUST NOT be implemented beyond an optional placeholder menu
143	  entry.
144	- The following actions are prohibited in this repository:
145	  - Changing the backend, its API contract, or its configuration.
146	  - Calling AI providers directly from the app.
147	  - Writing visual values (colors, font sizes, spacing, radii) outside
148	    `design_tokens.dart`.
149	  - Implementing extension features.
150	  - Committing `.env` or any credential.
151	  - Editing files under `docs/input/`.
152	
153	## Governance
154	
155	This constitution supersedes any conflicting practice, template, or
156	instruction used in this repository. Every plan, spec, task list, and
157	review MUST verify compliance with these principles before work is
158	considered done; any deviation MUST be justified in writing in the relevant
159	artifact (plan or PR description) or the work MUST be rejected.
160	
161	**Amendment procedure**: amendments are proposed by editing this file,
162	describing the change and rationale, and are adopted once the project owner
163	accepts the change (commit to this file constitutes adoption in this
164	single-maintainer project). Each amendment MUST update the Sync Impact
165	Report at the top of this file and the version/date line below.
166	
167	**Versioning policy** (semantic versioning for this document):
168	- **MAJOR** — backward-incompatible governance or principle removal/
169	  redefinition.
170	- **MINOR** — a new principle or section added, or materially expanded
171	  guidance.
172	- **PATCH** — wording clarifications, typo fixes, non-semantic refinements.
173	
174	**Compliance review**: any change to `lib/` MUST be checked against the
175	Core Principles and Quality Standards above before merge; violations of
176	RNF06–RNF09 in particular are release blockers.
177	
178	**Version**: 1.0.0 | **Ratified**: 2026-10-11 | **Last Amended**: 2026-10-11

`lib/core/design_tokens.dart` is the single source of colors, typography,
spacing, and radii. No visual value MAY be hardcoded anywhere else. The UI
MUST be faithful to `docs/input/prototype/`. UI text MUST be in Portuguese,
exactly as written in the prototype; code identifiers, comments, and project
documentation MUST be in English.

Rationale: a single token source makes visual fidelity (RNF08) mechanically
checkable, and separating UI language (Portuguese, matching the frozen
prototype) from code language (English) keeps the codebase reviewable while
preserving the product's voice.

### V. Clean Architecture Folder Convention
Code MUST follow the folder convention:
```
lib/
  core/
  features/
    <feature>/
      data/
      domain/
      presentation/
```
The domain layer MUST comply with RNF06: zero layer violations — it MUST
NOT import `package:flutter` nor any class from a feature's `data/` layer.

Rationale: a fixed, enforced folder shape and a flutter/data-free domain
layer make the domain independently testable and keep business rules
portable regardless of UI or persistence choices.

## Quality Standards (RNF01–RNF09)

These targets from `docs/input/requirements.md` are binding quality gates:

- **RNF01 — Interaction latency**: a local action MUST be reflected in the
  UI in under 100 ms; any network call taking longer than 300 ms MUST show a
  loading indicator.
- **RNF02 — PII stripping**: performed backend-side via Claude Haiku 4.5
  with a structured prompt / tool use, not a dedicated NER model; the app
  implements no PII-detection logic of its own.
- **RNF03 — Zero data retention**: a backend-side policy; the app MUST NOT
  introduce its own retention beyond what the backend requires.
- **RNF04 — Row Level Security (RLS)**: enforced backend-side; the app MUST
  assume RLS is authoritative and MUST NEVER attempt to bypass it.
- **RNF05 — Hard delete of account and data (LGPD)**: the app MUST expose
  the account-deletion flow (`DELETE /account`) from Settings.
- **RNF06 — Zero layer violations**: see Principle V; 0 violations is the
  target.
- **RNF07 — Domain test coverage**: `lib/**/domain/**` MUST reach at least
  80% test coverage.
- **RNF08 — Visual fidelity**: every screen MUST match the prototype's
  color, typography, and spacing, with 0 hardcoded visual values outside
  `design_tokens.dart`.
- **RNF09 — Consistent network-error handling**: every repository MUST use
  the `Either<Failure, T>` pattern via `fpdart`; every write endpoint (5
  endpoints) MUST handle timeout, malformed response, and no-connection
  failures, each covered by `mocktail` tests (15 of 15 scenarios).

## Scope & Delivery Boundaries

- Functional requirements MUST be implemented in the delivery order given in
  `docs/input/requirements.md`.
- Extension features (section 2 of `requirements.md`) are explicitly out of
  scope and MUST NOT be implemented beyond an optional placeholder menu
  entry.
- The following actions are prohibited in this repository:
  - Changing the backend, its API contract, or its configuration.
  - Calling AI providers directly from the app.
  - Writing visual values (colors, font sizes, spacing, radii) outside
    `design_tokens.dart`.
  - Implementing extension features.
  - Committing `.env` or any credential.
  - Editing files under `docs/input/`.

## Governance

This constitution supersedes any conflicting practice, template, or
instruction used in this repository. Every plan, spec, task list, and
review MUST verify compliance with these principles before work is
considered done; any deviation MUST be justified in writing in the relevant
artifact (plan or PR description) or the work MUST be rejected.

**Amendment procedure**: amendments are proposed by editing this file,
describing the change and rationale, and are adopted once the project owner
accepts the change (commit to this file constitutes adoption in this
single-maintainer project). Each amendment MUST update the Sync Impact
Report at the top of this file and the version/date line below.

**Versioning policy** (semantic versioning for this document):
- **MAJOR** — backward-incompatible governance or principle removal/
  redefinition.
- **MINOR** — a new principle or section added, or materially expanded
  guidance.
- **PATCH** — wording clarifications, typo fixes, non-semantic refinements.

**Compliance review**: any change to `lib/` MUST be checked against the
Core Principles and Quality Standards above before merge; violations of
RNF06–RNF09 in particular are release blockers.

**Version**: 1.0.0 | **Ratified**: 2026-10-11 | **Last Amended**: 2026-10-11

1	# Cerne — Requirements and Screen Flow
2	
3	Cerne is a reflective-journaling mobile app with an AI assistant. The user records their day by text, audio or photo; a conversational agent consults those records (semantic search) to answer with context and to offer insights.
4	
5	This document is the product specification. The visual reference is the prototype in `docs/input/prototype/`; the backend API is documented in `docs/input/backend/`.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 1. Functional requirements
10	
11	### RF01 — Multimodal capture (text / audio / photo)
12	Data entry by text, real-time audio recording and photo upload — always through Screen 2 (Insertion Modal), which has a raw text field in addition to the microphone and the gallery. Every capture becomes a persisted record (`POST /entries`), **distinct from a chat message** (see the separation note in RF04).
13	
14	**Acceptance criteria:**
15	- The three modalities (text, audio, photo) result in the same persisted-entry format — none is treated structurally differently from the others after capture.
16	- Cancelling a capture midway (e.g., interrupting a recording) does not create a partial or empty entry.
17	
18	### RF02 — Speech-to-text / OCR processing
19	Transcription of audio (speech-to-text) and recognition of text in images (OCR) over the content captured in RF01.
20	
21	**Acceptance criteria:** four visible states — recording, processing, transcribed, transcription error.
22	
23	### RF03 — Biometric authentication vault
24	Access barrier via Face ID / Touch ID / PIN before exposing the user's data.
25	
26	**Acceptance criteria:**
27	- A biometric failure (e.g., fingerprint not recognized) offers PIN as an alternative, without locking the user out of the app.
28	- The app, sent to the background and resumed after 5 minutes, requires authentication again — it does not stay unlocked indefinitely (fixed value, not configurable by the user).
29	
30	### RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)
31	Continuous conversation with the AI agent, with semantic search over previous entries. **Chat messages are conversational and do not create journal entries automatically** — the only exception is the explicit save action described in RF10. Otherwise, the chat queries existing entries via RAG but does not write to them.
32	
33	**Acceptance criteria:**
34	- Three mandatory UI states: processing/streaming, error, complete response.
35	- If the response stream drops midway, the partial message stays visible with a failure indication (it does not disappear).
36	
37	### RF05 — Personal summary export
38	Generation of a narrative summary by AI (Claude Haiku 4.5) from the user's entries, exportable as PDF, with an additional option to download the raw data without the narrative. No clinical or diagnostic connotation. **Scope: job generation, file download and failure handling — never the quality of the generated narrative text.**
39	
40	**Acceptance criteria:**
41	- An export job with zero entries in the period returns a handled error state (not an empty PDF, not a crash).
42	- A failure generating the narrative text (model timeout) still allows downloading the raw data without the narrative — the export is not blocked by an AI failure.
43	
44	### RF06 — Semantic search / filter over journal entries
45	Semantic similarity search (via Voyage AI embeddings, reusing the ones already generated in RF01) combined with metadata filters (date, entry type). There is no filter by tag or category: the backend does not implement it in any endpoint — `GET /entries` and `GET /entries/search` accept only `source` and `dateFrom`/`dateTo`. Tags appear only embedded, read-only, in the `Entry` object (see section 2).
46	
47	**Acceptance criteria:**
48	- Searching for a term finds semantically related entries even without the exact word (e.g., searching "ansiedade" returns an entry that only mentions "nervosismo", without the literal term).
49	- 300 ms search debounce: fast typing triggers a single query, not one per keystroke.
50	- Results from the local read cache stay consistent with the server after reconnection, without duplicating displayed items *(the architecture is cloud-only; offline allows only viewing already-cached data, not writing)*.
51	- Two or more filters applied at the same time (`source` + `dateFrom`/`dateTo`) narrow results with AND logic (not OR).
52	- Clearing the filters returns to the full list without restarting the screen.
53	
54	### RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline)
55	A screen whose state depends simultaneously on authentication, synchronization status and entry data.
56	
57	**Acceptance criteria:**
58	- Session expiration while viewing triggers a new-login prompt without a crash and without losing the scroll position.
59	- The per-entry synchronization status badge updates independently of the authentication stream.
60	- No BLoC imports another BLoC directly.
61	
62	### RF08 — Proactive insights (mechanism)
63	A suggestion inserted into the chat without the user asking for it. **Scope: only the trigger mechanism, never the quality of the generated text.**
64	
65	**Acceptance criteria:**
66	- Trigger after N = 5 user messages OR T = 2 min of inactivity — fires exactly once per satisfied condition.
67	- If insight generation fails (timeout / network error), the main chat keeps working normally.
68	- Dismissing the insight does not change the scroll position or the state of the main conversation.
69	
70	### RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard
71	An evolution chart with a textual summary, computed on demand when the Settings tab is opened. **Scope: aggregation and rendering, never the quality of the narrative text.**
72	
73	**Acceptance criteria:**
74	- Renders correctly in three scenarios: zero entries, one entry, more than 30 entries.
75	- The aggregation recalculates correctly after an entry is created (cache-invalidation test). Entries are immutable: there is no `PATCH /entries/:id` or `DELETE /entries/:id` in the backend, and no screen describes an edit or delete action on an entry.
76	- The AI narrative text is checked only for not breaking the UI in extreme cases — never for its content.
77	
78	### RF10 — Save a chat message as an entry
79	A button on each user message in the chat that converts it into a persisted entry — for moments when the user states relevant information during the conversation, not only through dedicated capture (RF01). It reuses the same `POST /entries` pipeline (PII check + embedding), with the origin marked as `chat`.
80	
81	**Acceptance criteria:**
82	- The chat feature triggers the creation of the entry through a shared interface / use case, never by directly importing a repository or data source of the entries feature — a violation here also breaks RNF06.
83	- Saving the same message twice does not create duplicate entries (idempotency).
84	- A failure to save (network unavailable) keeps the conversation working normally, and the button returns to a state that allows trying again — the same failure-isolation pattern as RF08.
85	- Only user messages have the button — AI responses cannot become entries.
86	
87	---
88	
89	## 2. Extension features — not implemented
90	
91	They keep the "essence" of the original product flow and exist in the prototype, but **receive no functional implementation**. A menu entry may exist as a placeholder.
92	
93	| Original feature | Treatment in the current version |
94	|---|---|
95	| Dynamic categorization (AI) | Simplified to manual tags created by the user (My Records screen) |
96	| Autonomous goal extraction | Action Plans screen — static, no logic |
97	| Dynamic persona adjustment | Simple cosmetic toggle (Settings), low cost to maintain |
98	
99	---
100	
101	## 3. Quality requirements
102	
103	| ID | Requirement | Target |
104	|---|---|---|
105	| RNF06 | Zero layer violations — the domain layer does not import `package:flutter` nor classes from `data/` | 0 violations |
106	| RNF07 | Minimum test coverage of the domain layer (`lib/**/domain/**`) | ≥ 80% |
107	| RNF08 | Visual fidelity to the prototype — the primary color matches the prototype's hex value, typography matches family and size, spacing matches the prototype; no visual value hardcoded outside the central file `design_tokens.dart` | Every screen faithful in color, typography and spacing; 0 hardcoded values |
108	| RNF09 | Consistent network-error handling — `Either<Failure, T>` pattern via `fpdart` in every repository; every write endpoint (5 endpoints) handles three failure types — timeout, malformed response, no connection — covered by tests with `mocktail` | 0 repository signatures outside the pattern; 15 of 15 scenarios handled |
109	
110	## 4. Other non-functional requirements
111	
112	RNF01 — Interaction latency (a local action is reflected in the UI in < 100 ms; any network call above 300 ms shows a loading indicator) · RNF02 — PII stripping (via Claude Haiku 4.5 with a structured prompt / tool use, not a dedicated NER model) · RNF03 — Zero data retention · RNF04 — RLS (Row Level Security) · RNF05 — Hard delete of account and data (LGPD).
113	
114	**Known limitation:** the system has no protocol for detecting or responding to risk signals (suicidal ideation, self-harm) in entries or chat messages. Since the product is not framed as a mental-health app, this absence is an explicit scope decision.
115	
116	---
117	
118	## 5. Interface architecture and screen flow
119	
120	### 5.1 Visual foundation (design system)
121	Minimalist identity, a warm and neutral palette, readable sans-serif typography, standardized components (buttons, chat bubbles, cards). This foundation is the direct object of RNF08. Tokens: `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md`.
122	
123	### 5.2 Screens
124	
125	**Screen 0 — Splash:** initial loading; checks the connection and syncs the cache in the background. *Connects to: RF06, RNF01.*
126	
127	**Screen 0.1 — Authentication vault:** biometric/PIN barrier before access. *Connects to: RF03.*
128	
129	**Screen 1 — Home (chat):** main screen, continuous conversation, "+" button for multimodal input, AI status indicator, "save to journal" button on each user message. *Connects to: RF04, RF08, RF10, RNF01, RNF09.*
130	
131	**Screen 2 — Insertion Modal:** overlay with three ways to capture — raw text field, microphone (audio) and gallery/camera (photo) — with a transcription indicator. Every capture here creates a persisted entry, never a chat message. *Connects to: RF01, RF02.*
132	
133	**Screen 3 — Side menu (sidebar):** navigation hub, session history, access to My Records / Action Plans / Settings, and a "Novo Chat" button that opens Screen 1 in its empty state. *Connects to: RF04 (via the "Novo Chat" button); the other items are pure navigation.*
134	
135	**Screen 4 — My Records:** consolidated timeline, filters, manual tags (extension, section 2), export. *Connects to: RF07, RF06, RF05.*
136	
137	**Screen 5 — Action Plans:** simple Kanban board (columns "A Fazer" / "Em Andamento" / "Concluído") with static example cards. *(Extension — section 2.)*
138	
139	**Screen 6 — Settings and profile:** evolution dashboard, persona selector — "Analítico" / "Empático" / "Socrático" (extension, section 2; it would only change the system-prompt string of RF04), delete account. *Connects to: RF09, RNF05.*
140	
141	---
142	
143	## 6. Backend endpoint inventory
144	
145	The backend is already built and frozen. The API contract, `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`, is the source of truth; this section is a reading of it oriented by screen and requirement. How to build the real URL of each operation: `docs/input/backend/README.md`.
146	
147	Every endpoint returns errors in the standard contract of RNF09 — `{ code, message, retryable }` — and is protected by RLS in Supabase. AI providers: Claude (chat, vision/OCR, summary, insights, dashboard, PII detection) and Voyage AI (embeddings) — the backend's only two external AI dependencies. Audio transcription (speech-to-text) runs on-device (Whisper) and never reaches the backend as an audio file.
148	
149	### 6.1 Authentication and session
150	| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
151	|---|---|---|
152	| `POST /auth/signup` | RF03 | — |
153	| `POST /auth/login` | RF03 | — |
154	| `POST /auth/refresh` | RF03, RF07 | — |
155	| `GET /auth/session` | RF07 | — |
156	| `POST /auth/logout` | RF03 | — |
157	
158	**No "biometric-unlock" endpoint — intentional:** the Face ID / Touch ID / PIN barrier of Screen 0.1 is validated entirely on the device, never on the server. The backend only stores the preference (`biometricEnabled`, read and written via `PATCH /account/settings`, section 6.7) — it validates no biometrics. After passing the local barrier, the app uses the existing session (renewed via `POST /auth/refresh` when needed, or `POST /auth/login` if it has fully expired).
159	
160	### 6.2 Ingestion and entries
161	| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
162	|---|---|---|
163	| `POST /media/ocr` — the image is not persisted; only the extracted text moves on | RF02 | Claude Haiku 4.5 (vision) |
164	| `POST /entries` — creates an entry; internally triggers the PII check and embedding generation; accepts `source` (`manual`/`audio`/`photo`/`chat`) and `chatMessageId` when the origin is the chat | RF01, RF02, RF10 | Claude Haiku 4.5 (PII) + Voyage AI (embedding) |
165	| `GET /entries` — filters by `source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo`; tags appear only embedded in the response, read-only | RF07 | — |
166	| `GET /entries/:id` | RF07 | — |
167	
168	**No entry editing or deletion, and no tag endpoint — intentional:** entries are immutable once created ("original content intact, never censored"); there is no `PATCH`/`DELETE /entries/:id`. Tags are populated only by test seed data — no endpoint creates, deletes or filters by tag or category (see RF06). This is consistent with section 2: dynamic categorization was simplified to manual tags that receive no functional implementation.
169	
170	### 6.3 Chat and memory (RAG)
171	| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
172	|---|---|---|
173	| `POST /chat/sessions` — blocked offline | RF04 | — |
174	| `GET /chat/sessions` — works offline (cache) | RF04, RF07 | — |
175	| `GET /chat/sessions/:id/messages` — works offline (cache) | RF04 | — |
176	| `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages` — streaming (SSE); blocked offline | RF04 | Voyage AI (question embedding) + Claude Sonnet 5 (response) |
177	| `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages/:userMessageId/retry` — regenerates the response without duplicating the user's question; it supports "partial message visible with a failure indication, and a way to try again" in RF04 | RF04 | Voyage AI (embedding, reused from cache) + Claude Sonnet 5 (response) |
178	| `POST /chat/sessions/:id/insight` | RF08 | Claude Haiku 4.5 |
179	| `POST /entries` — called from the "save to journal" button (see 6.2) | RF10 | Claude Haiku 4.5 (PII) + Voyage AI (embedding) |
180	
181	### 6.4 Search
182	| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
183	|---|---|---|
184	| `GET /entries/search?q=&source=&dateFrom=&dateTo=&limit=` — no `category` (see RF06) | RF06 | Voyage AI (query embedding) |
185	
186	### 6.5 Export
187	| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
188	|---|---|---|
189	| `POST /export/summary` — asynchronous job | RF05 | Claude Haiku 4.5 |
190	| `GET /export/:jobId/status` | RF05 | — |
191	| `GET /export/:jobId/download` | RF05 | — |
192	
193	### 6.6 Dashboard
194	| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
195	|---|---|---|
196	| `GET /dashboard/aggregate?period=` — separate from the text so it does not block the chart | RF09 | — |

# Cerne — Requirements and Screen Flow

Cerne is a reflective-journaling mobile app with an AI assistant. The user records their day by text, audio or photo; a conversational agent consults those records (semantic search) to answer with context and to offer insights.

This document is the product specification. The visual reference is the prototype in `docs/input/prototype/`; the backend API is documented in `docs/input/backend/`.

---

## 1. Functional requirements

### RF01 — Multimodal capture (text / audio / photo)
Data entry by text, real-time audio recording and photo upload — always through Screen 2 (Insertion Modal), which has a raw text field in addition to the microphone and the gallery. Every capture becomes a persisted record (`POST /entries`), **distinct from a chat message** (see the separation note in RF04).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- The three modalities (text, audio, photo) result in the same persisted-entry format — none is treated structurally differently from the others after capture.
- Cancelling a capture midway (e.g., interrupting a recording) does not create a partial or empty entry.

### RF02 — Speech-to-text / OCR processing
Transcription of audio (speech-to-text) and recognition of text in images (OCR) over the content captured in RF01.

**Acceptance criteria:** four visible states — recording, processing, transcribed, transcription error.

### RF03 — Biometric authentication vault
Access barrier via Face ID / Touch ID / PIN before exposing the user's data.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- A biometric failure (e.g., fingerprint not recognized) offers PIN as an alternative, without locking the user out of the app.
- The app, sent to the background and resumed after 5 minutes, requires authentication again — it does not stay unlocked indefinitely (fixed value, not configurable by the user).

### RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)
Continuous conversation with the AI agent, with semantic search over previous entries. **Chat messages are conversational and do not create journal entries automatically** — the only exception is the explicit save action described in RF10. Otherwise, the chat queries existing entries via RAG but does not write to them.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Three mandatory UI states: processing/streaming, error, complete response.
- If the response stream drops midway, the partial message stays visible with a failure indication (it does not disappear).

### RF05 — Personal summary export
Generation of a narrative summary by AI (Claude Haiku 4.5) from the user's entries, exportable as PDF, with an additional option to download the raw data without the narrative. No clinical or diagnostic connotation. **Scope: job generation, file download and failure handling — never the quality of the generated narrative text.**

**Acceptance criteria:**
- An export job with zero entries in the period returns a handled error state (not an empty PDF, not a crash).
- A failure generating the narrative text (model timeout) still allows downloading the raw data without the narrative — the export is not blocked by an AI failure.

### RF06 — Semantic search / filter over journal entries
Semantic similarity search (via Voyage AI embeddings, reusing the ones already generated in RF01) combined with metadata filters (date, entry type). There is no filter by tag or category: the backend does not implement it in any endpoint — `GET /entries` and `GET /entries/search` accept only `source` and `dateFrom`/`dateTo`. Tags appear only embedded, read-only, in the `Entry` object (see section 2).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Searching for a term finds semantically related entries even without the exact word (e.g., searching "ansiedade" returns an entry that only mentions "nervosismo", without the literal term).
- 300 ms search debounce: fast typing triggers a single query, not one per keystroke.
- Results from the local read cache stay consistent with the server after reconnection, without duplicating displayed items *(the architecture is cloud-only; offline allows only viewing already-cached data, not writing)*.
- Two or more filters applied at the same time (`source` + `dateFrom`/`dateTo`) narrow results with AND logic (not OR).
- Clearing the filters returns to the full list without restarting the screen.

### RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline)
A screen whose state depends simultaneously on authentication, synchronization status and entry data.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Session expiration while viewing triggers a new-login prompt without a crash and without losing the scroll position.
- The per-entry synchronization status badge updates independently of the authentication stream.
- No BLoC imports another BLoC directly.

### RF08 — Proactive insights (mechanism)
A suggestion inserted into the chat without the user asking for it. **Scope: only the trigger mechanism, never the quality of the generated text.**

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Trigger after N = 5 user messages OR T = 2 min of inactivity — fires exactly once per satisfied condition.
- If insight generation fails (timeout / network error), the main chat keeps working normally.
- Dismissing the insight does not change the scroll position or the state of the main conversation.

### RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard
An evolution chart with a textual summary, computed on demand when the Settings tab is opened. **Scope: aggregation and rendering, never the quality of the narrative text.**

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Renders correctly in three scenarios: zero entries, one entry, more than 30 entries.
- The aggregation recalculates correctly after an entry is created (cache-invalidation test). Entries are immutable: there is no `PATCH /entries/:id` or `DELETE /entries/:id` in the backend, and no screen describes an edit or delete action on an entry.
- The AI narrative text is checked only for not breaking the UI in extreme cases — never for its content.

### RF10 — Save a chat message as an entry
A button on each user message in the chat that converts it into a persisted entry — for moments when the user states relevant information during the conversation, not only through dedicated capture (RF01). It reuses the same `POST /entries` pipeline (PII check + embedding), with the origin marked as `chat`.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- The chat feature triggers the creation of the entry through a shared interface / use case, never by directly importing a repository or data source of the entries feature — a violation here also breaks RNF06.
- Saving the same message twice does not create duplicate entries (idempotency).
- A failure to save (network unavailable) keeps the conversation working normally, and the button returns to a state that allows trying again — the same failure-isolation pattern as RF08.
- Only user messages have the button — AI responses cannot become entries.

---

## 2. Extension features — not implemented

They keep the "essence" of the original product flow and exist in the prototype, but **receive no functional implementation**. A menu entry may exist as a placeholder.

| Original feature | Treatment in the current version |
|---|---|
| Dynamic categorization (AI) | Simplified to manual tags created by the user (My Records screen) |
| Autonomous goal extraction | Action Plans screen — static, no logic |
| Dynamic persona adjustment | Simple cosmetic toggle (Settings), low cost to maintain |

---

## 3. Quality requirements

| ID | Requirement | Target |
|---|---|---|
| RNF06 | Zero layer violations — the domain layer does not import `package:flutter` nor classes from `data/` | 0 violations |
| RNF07 | Minimum test coverage of the domain layer (`lib/**/domain/**`) | ≥ 80% |
| RNF08 | Visual fidelity to the prototype — the primary color matches the prototype's hex value, typography matches family and size, spacing matches the prototype; no visual value hardcoded outside the central file `design_tokens.dart` | Every screen faithful in color, typography and spacing; 0 hardcoded values |
| RNF09 | Consistent network-error handling — `Either<Failure, T>` pattern via `fpdart` in every repository; every write endpoint (5 endpoints) handles three failure types — timeout, malformed response, no connection — covered by tests with `mocktail` | 0 repository signatures outside the pattern; 15 of 15 scenarios handled |

## 4. Other non-functional requirements

RNF01 — Interaction latency (a local action is reflected in the UI in < 100 ms; any network call above 300 ms shows a loading indicator) · RNF02 — PII stripping (via Claude Haiku 4.5 with a structured prompt / tool use, not a dedicated NER model) · RNF03 — Zero data retention · RNF04 — RLS (Row Level Security) · RNF05 — Hard delete of account and data (LGPD).

**Known limitation:** the system has no protocol for detecting or responding to risk signals (suicidal ideation, self-harm) in entries or chat messages. Since the product is not framed as a mental-health app, this absence is an explicit scope decision.

---

## 5. Interface architecture and screen flow

### 5.1 Visual foundation (design system)
Minimalist identity, a warm and neutral palette, readable sans-serif typography, standardized components (buttons, chat bubbles, cards). This foundation is the direct object of RNF08. Tokens: `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md`.

### 5.2 Screens

**Screen 0 — Splash:** initial loading; checks the connection and syncs the cache in the background. *Connects to: RF06, RNF01.*

**Screen 0.1 — Authentication vault:** biometric/PIN barrier before access. *Connects to: RF03.*

**Screen 1 — Home (chat):** main screen, continuous conversation, "+" button for multimodal input, AI status indicator, "save to journal" button on each user message. *Connects to: RF04, RF08, RF10, RNF01, RNF09.*

**Screen 2 — Insertion Modal:** overlay with three ways to capture — raw text field, microphone (audio) and gallery/camera (photo) — with a transcription indicator. Every capture here creates a persisted entry, never a chat message. *Connects to: RF01, RF02.*

**Screen 3 — Side menu (sidebar):** navigation hub, session history, access to My Records / Action Plans / Settings, and a "Novo Chat" button that opens Screen 1 in its empty state. *Connects to: RF04 (via the "Novo Chat" button); the other items are pure navigation.*

**Screen 4 — My Records:** consolidated timeline, filters, manual tags (extension, section 2), export. *Connects to: RF07, RF06, RF05.*

**Screen 5 — Action Plans:** simple Kanban board (columns "A Fazer" / "Em Andamento" / "Concluído") with static example cards. *(Extension — section 2.)*

**Screen 6 — Settings and profile:** evolution dashboard, persona selector — "Analítico" / "Empático" / "Socrático" (extension, section 2; it would only change the system-prompt string of RF04), delete account. *Connects to: RF09, RNF05.*

---

## 6. Backend endpoint inventory

The backend is already built and frozen. The API contract, `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`, is the source of truth; this section is a reading of it oriented by screen and requirement. How to build the real URL of each operation: `docs/input/backend/README.md`.

Every endpoint returns errors in the standard contract of RNF09 — `{ code, message, retryable }` — and is protected by RLS in Supabase. AI providers: Claude (chat, vision/OCR, summary, insights, dashboard, PII detection) and Voyage AI (embeddings) — the backend's only two external AI dependencies. Audio transcription (speech-to-text) runs on-device (Whisper) and never reaches the backend as an audio file.

### 6.1 Authentication and session
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /auth/signup` | RF03 | — |
| `POST /auth/login` | RF03 | — |
| `POST /auth/refresh` | RF03, RF07 | — |
| `GET /auth/session` | RF07 | — |
| `POST /auth/logout` | RF03 | — |

**No "biometric-unlock" endpoint — intentional:** the Face ID / Touch ID / PIN barrier of Screen 0.1 is validated entirely on the device, never on the server. The backend only stores the preference (`biometricEnabled`, read and written via `PATCH /account/settings`, section 6.7) — it validates no biometrics. After passing the local barrier, the app uses the existing session (renewed via `POST /auth/refresh` when needed, or `POST /auth/login` if it has fully expired).

### 6.2 Ingestion and entries
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /media/ocr` — the image is not persisted; only the extracted text moves on | RF02 | Claude Haiku 4.5 (vision) |
| `POST /entries` — creates an entry; internally triggers the PII check and embedding generation; accepts `source` (`manual`/`audio`/`photo`/`chat`) and `chatMessageId` when the origin is the chat | RF01, RF02, RF10 | Claude Haiku 4.5 (PII) + Voyage AI (embedding) |
| `GET /entries` — filters by `source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo`; tags appear only embedded in the response, read-only | RF07 | — |
| `GET /entries/:id` | RF07 | — |

**No entry editing or deletion, and no tag endpoint — intentional:** entries are immutable once created ("original content intact, never censored"); there is no `PATCH`/`DELETE /entries/:id`. Tags are populated only by test seed data — no endpoint creates, deletes or filters by tag or category (see RF06). This is consistent with section 2: dynamic categorization was simplified to manual tags that receive no functional implementation.

### 6.3 Chat and memory (RAG)
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /chat/sessions` — blocked offline | RF04 | — |
| `GET /chat/sessions` — works offline (cache) | RF04, RF07 | — |
| `GET /chat/sessions/:id/messages` — works offline (cache) | RF04 | — |
| `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages` — streaming (SSE); blocked offline | RF04 | Voyage AI (question embedding) + Claude Sonnet 5 (response) |
| `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages/:userMessageId/retry` — regenerates the response without duplicating the user's question; it supports "partial message visible with a failure indication, and a way to try again" in RF04 | RF04 | Voyage AI (embedding, reused from cache) + Claude Sonnet 5 (response) |
| `POST /chat/sessions/:id/insight` | RF08 | Claude Haiku 4.5 |
| `POST /entries` — called from the "save to journal" button (see 6.2) | RF10 | Claude Haiku 4.5 (PII) + Voyage AI (embedding) |

### 6.4 Search
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /entries/search?q=&source=&dateFrom=&dateTo=&limit=` — no `category` (see RF06) | RF06 | Voyage AI (query embedding) |

### 6.5 Export

|---|---|---|
| `POST /export/summary` — asynchronous job | RF05 | Claude Haiku 4.5 |
| `GET /export/:jobId/status` | RF05 | — |
| `GET /export/:jobId/download` | RF05 | — |

### 6.6 Dashboard

| `GET /dashboard/aggregate?period=` — separate from the text so it does not block the chart | RF09 | — |
| `GET /dashboard/narrative?period=` | RF09 | Claude Haiku 4.5 |

### 6.7 Account
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `PATCH /account/settings` — includes the persona toggle (extension) | RNF05, extension | — |
| `DELETE /account` | RNF05 | — |

|---|---|---|
| Background session timeout | 5 min | RF03 |
| Search debounce | 300 ms | RF06 |
| Proactive insight trigger | 5 messages OR 2 min of inactivity | RF08 |
| Dashboard rendering scenarios | 0 / 1 / > 30 entries | RF09 |
| Minimum test coverage (domain) | ≥ 80% | RNF07 |
| Local UI latency | < 100 ms | RNF01 |
| Loading-indicator threshold | > 300 ms | RNF01 |
| Network-error scenarios tested | 5 endpoints × 3 failures = 15 | RNF09 |

---

## 11. Error codes (RNF09)

Every endpoint returns `{ code, message, retryable }`. Minimum codes the app handles:

| Code | Situation | `retryable` |
|---|---|---|
| `AUTH_EXPIRED` | Session expired, re-authentication needed | no |
| `AUTH_INVALID` | Invalid credentials / biometrics | no |
| `NETWORK_TIMEOUT` | Request exceeded the time limit | yes |
| `NETWORK_OFFLINE` | No connection — action blocked (see RF04/RF06) | yes |
| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | Malformed request body | no |
| `PII_CHECK_FAILED` | PII check failed before persisting | yes |
| `EMBEDDING_FAILED` | Voyage AI unavailable / error | yes |
| `AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT` | Claude did not respond in time (chat/insight/summary/dashboard) | yes |
| `NOT_FOUND` | Resource does not exist or does not belong to the user | no |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | Request limit exceeded | yes |

The complete, closed list of the backend's 13 codes, with HTTP statuses, is in `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md`.

---

## 12. Delivery order

Work is delivered in units, one per functional requirement, preceded by a foundation unit, in this order:

**F000 → RF03 → RF01 → RF02 → RF07 → RF06 → RF04 → RF10 → RF08 → RF05 → RF09**

- **F000 (foundation)** covers what no single requirement owns but all of them use: project scaffold, `design_tokens.dart`, HTTP client returning `Either`, login and sign-up (Screen 0.1a in the prototype), base navigation and expired-session handling.
- RF10 comes after RF01 and RF04; RF08 comes after RF04.

---

## 13. Technical constraints

**Fixed:**
- Flutter and Dart at the version pinned for the repository (fvm).
- State management: `flutter_bloc`.
- Clean Architecture, three layers per feature.
- Error handling: `fpdart`; repositories return `Either<Failure, T>`.
- Test doubles: `mocktail`.
- On-device speech-to-text: `whisper_ggml`.
- Visual tokens: `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` is the single source of colors, typography, spacing and radii.
- Platform: iOS, portrait only.
- Folder convention:

```
lib/
  core/
  features/
    <feature>/
      data/
      domain/
      presentation/
```

**Free (choose what fits):** routing, HTTP client, local cache, dependency injection, secure storage, biometrics package, chart package.
